2607.04738.title: Wasserstein Residuals: Learning Gradient Flows from Population Dynamics
2607.04738.paper_summary: Reconstructing population dynamics is a central problem in the physical and data sciences. Often, the dynamics are modeled as a Wasserstein gradient flow (WGF): a curve of distributions driven by an energy functional. Though there are multiple mathematical characterizations of a WGF, the dominant algorithmic approach relies on the Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) scheme. JKO-based methods are inflexible to time discretisation and require solving costly optimal transport problems. We take a residual approach, enforcing the continuity equations via a non-negative loss function whose minimum is the WGF. Combined with a data-fitting divergence, this gives a single global objective. This perspective unifies several existing methods and leads to a new particle-based method, stitching, that is simulation-free and robust to large gaps between observations. We demonstrate that the stitching method achieves state-of-the-art performance across trajectory inference benchmarks. For code see github.com/BasisResearch/wasserstein-residuals.
2607.04738.paper_summary_zh: 重建人口動態是物理和數據科學中的一個核心問題。通常，這些動態被建模為Wasserstein梯度流（WGF）：由能量泛函驅動的分佈曲線。雖然對WGF有多種數學表徵，但主導的算法方法依賴於Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto（JKO）方案。基於JKO的方法對時間離散化不夠靈活，並且需要解決成本高昂的最佳運輸問題。我們採取了一種殘差方法，通過一個非負損失函數強制執行連續性方程，其最小值即為WGF。結合數據擬合的散度，這提供了一個單一的全局目標。這種觀點統一了幾種現有方法，並導致了一種新的基於粒子的方法——拼接，該方法無需模擬，並對觀測之間的大間隙具有魯棒性。我們證明拼接方法在軌跡推斷基準測試中達到了最先進的性能。代碼請參見github.com/BasisResearch/wasserstein-residuals。
